title: High-cutoff residual-basis conditioning diagnostic
question: Does the R-426 residual-reuse mismatch at the fixed high-cutoff row arise from a conditioning-amplified basis representation difference, or does it persist as an algebraic disagreement after basis-invariant cross-checks?

new_perspective.principle: Keep the R-426 failing row and 5e-7 comparison tolerance fixed while comparing the residual subspace through independent orthonormal bases and an explicit constraint projector.
route: Reconstruct the R-426 row from the hash-pinned R-419, R-416 and R-422 parents without importing the R-426 primary output.
Compute the R-422 blockwise weighted-zero-mean basis, the R-406 block-complement basis, a constraint-projector nullspace basis and a Householder QR nullspace basis.
Measure orthogonality, block-constraint residuals, cross-Gram singular values, projector distance, operator norm and the first residual Rayleigh value for every basis.
Compare the fixed R-426 residual-reuse difference with the conditioning amplification budget; classify only as an inconclusive diagnostic unless a precision-certified invariant value is obtained.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A conditioning diagnostic identifies a finite numerical boundary for a future analytic common-core estimate; it does not prove a cutoff-uniform gap, a physical sector or any Yang-Mills statement.

metrics: positive normalized weights and reversible conductance

assumptions: The hash-pinned R-419 conditional law, R-416 log-domain row and R-422/R-406 finite basis constructions are the declared inputs.
The fixed R-426 row and comparison tolerance are not changed during the diagnostic.
The normalized constraint rows represent the same blockwise weighted-zero-mean residual subspace in exact arithmetic.
A two-norm perturbation budget is recorded as a conditioning diagnostic, not promoted as a certified error bound for the underlying eigensolver.
Double-precision basis agreement cannot by itself certify the exact residual gap when the operator norm is large.
missing_assumptions: An arbitrary-precision or interval-certified eigensolve for the failing residual subspace.
A basis-independent exact or rigorously bounded residual-reuse value at the high cutoff.
A common unbounded Q3 Hamiltonian core and a cutoff/volume-uniform perturbation estimate.
Transfer of any repaired finite residual value through history, OS/KMS/GNS and physical-sector interfaces.
stop_conditions: If the independent bases violate the fixed projector/constraint tolerances, classify the route as a construction failure and retain R-426.
If the conditioning budget is below the fixed mismatch, do not label the mismatch conditioning-supported; retain an algebraic/inconclusive boundary.
Do not relax the R-426 comparison tolerance, clip a residual or promote a finite diagnostic to a uniform theorem.
evidence_level: T0 / EXECUTED FINITE CONDITIONING AND BASIS-CROSSWALK DIAGNOSTIC; the cause of the R-426 mismatch remains inconclusive and no residual-reuse closure is claimed
non_claims: No repair or closure of the R-426 residual-reuse failure.
No proof that the mismatch is solely floating-point roundoff or solely algebraic.
No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform Schur/residual bound.
No common core, history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, sector gap or continuum limit.
No C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
boundary: R-428 reconstructs one R-426 high-cutoff residual row and quantifies basis conditioning. The residual subspace projectors agree to near machine precision while the operator norm creates an amplification budget larger than the fixed comparison tolerance; without precision certification the route remains INCONCLUSIVE_CONDITIONING and R-426's failure is preserved.
next_unlock: Implement an arbitrary-precision or interval-certified basis-invariant residual eigensolve for the fixed row, compare it with the R-422 value without changing tolerance, and only then decide whether residual reuse can be repaired.

lean_crosscheck.role: R428 Lean checks only the finite scalar diagnostic inequalities; Python carries the matrix reconstruction.
